newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Mitsui to modernise Uzbek oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui to modernise Uzbek oil refinery.

text.p: Japan's Mitsui Corp is close to signing a $200 million contract to modernise Uzbekistan's Fergana oil refinery, a spokesman for Mitsui said in the Uzbek capital Tashkent on Wednesday.
"The contract will be signed between Mitsui and Uzbekneftegaz at the end of August or the beginning of September," the spokesman told Reuters. Uzbekneftegaz is Uzbekistan's state-owned oil company.
The Mitsui spokesman said a mission from Japan's Eximbank will visit Tashkent next week to finalise details of a $120 million credit for the project.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development will provide the remaining $80 million, he said.
The work is planned to take 30-33 months to complete, with work subcontracted out to Toyo Engineering Corp.
Current capacity of the refinery, the only one operating in the desert nation of 22 million and located around 300 km (200 miles) north of Tashkent, is around six million tonnes a year.
The work is needed in part to convert the refinery from processing imported Russian oil to Uzbekistan's own crude from its rich Kokdumalak field.
Supplies of Russian crude to the Fergana refinery fell to 0.5 million tonnes in 1995 from 2.7 million tonnes in 1994.
A second oil refinery in Uzbekistan's Bukhara region, with a capacity of five million tonnes a year, is currently under construction by French firm Technip.
